title: Collision/bijection static checker: fails CI on unsupported strict reversibility claims
context: A false strict reversibility claim silently corrupts downstream data: a name romanized to Latin cannot be exactly recovered to Cyrillic. The collision/bijection checker prevents this by statically analyzing a scheme's rule set for many-to-one target collisions and unresolved context overlaps before any data is published. If a scheme is tagged reversibility: strict but the checker finds an ambiguous inverse, the build must fail. This is a hard gate, not advisory output.
objective: Implement a static collision/bijection checker (checkReversible(schemeId) or as a standalone CLI gate) that analyzes a mapping scheme's rule set, detects many-to-one target collisions and unresolvable context overlaps for the inverse direction, emits a structured report of whether strict reversibility is achievable, and exits non-zero (failing CI) if a scheme tagged reversibility: strict has any unresolvable collision.
acceptanceCriteria: checkReversible(schemeId) returns a structured report: { achievable: boolean, collisions: Array<{from, to, conflicts}>, contextOverlaps: Array<{...}> }
The checker exits non-zero and prints a human-readable failure message in CI when a strict-tagged scheme has any detected collision or unresolvable context overlap
The checker correctly reports achievable: true for a clean bijective rule set (no two source tokens map to the same target token, no unresolvable context ambiguity in the inverse direction)
The checker correctly reports achievable: false for a rule set with known collisions (tested with a synthetic scheme containing deliberate many-to-one mappings)
Integrated into pnpm test so it runs automatically on every scheme in data/schemes/; schemes tagged strict must pass, others get a warning only
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint passes
output: packages/core/src/checker.ts (or equivalent) + integration in pnpm test; test cases covering clean and collision-containing synthetic schemes
